property_summary: When transfer is called with _tos = [address(0x1)], the reference contract makes one external call to caddress.transferFrom(from, 0x1, v) (reverting if caddress lacks the function), but the mutant makes zero calls because the loop condition i < 0 is never true, leading to different state: the reference reverts (if the external call fails) while the mutant always returns true.

When transfer is called with _tos = [address(0x1)], v = 0, and caddress = address(this) (which lacks transferFrom), the reference contract reverts due to the external call failure, while the mutant returns true without making any calls.

When transfer is called with _tos = [address(0x1)], v = 0, and caddress = address(this) (which lacks transferFrom), the reference contract reverts due to the external call failure, while the mutant returns true without making any calls.

Call transfer with _tos containing one address and caddress set to a contract that always reverts on any call; the reference reverts due to the external call failure, while the buggy version (loop condition i<0) returns true silently.

With _tos = [address(0x1)], v = 0, caddress = address(this) (which lacks transferFrom), the reference contract reverts due to the failed external call, while the mutant returns true because the loop never executes.

After a call to transfer(address,address,address[],uint256) with from=0xAlice, caddress=a mock token contract, _tos=[0xBob], v=100, the reference C calls transferFrom on the mock token (which emits an event), while the buggy version calls the wrong selector transfer (which does nothing). The divergence is observed by checking the mock token's lastCalledSelector public variable: reference returns bytes4 of transferFrom, bug returns bytes4 of transfer.
After transfer with from=0xAlice, caddress=0xToken, _tos=[0xBob], v=100, reference sets balance[0xBob] to 100 via transferFrom, bug sets balance[0xBob] to 0 because wrong selector.

After calling transfer with a single recipient and a non-zero value, the reference contract's function returns true, but the buggy version returns false; the test catches that by asserting the return value of the call.
